findings.description: Nit: After adjudication, Atlas Symbol Tree Export still has normative SHALLs without dedicated WHEN/THEN coverage (Rule Group 2). Still uncovered: exact `<name>  (<file>:<line>)  [<kind>]` line shape; secondary sort by id (Callees scenario only says sorted by name); target-resolution precedence (exact id → unique name → file path/basename) beyond basename; stdlib-only / no-network; and—in design D3 but missing from the requirement body—`--direction both` emitting labelled `callees:` / `callers:` sections (the Non-call edges scenario already depends on `callees:`). Either add scenarios (and put the `both` section headers into the SHALL body) or demote non-behavioral constraints out of SHALL language.

findings.description: Nit: Design D3 states that `--direction both` prints labelled sections `callees:` / `callers:`, and scenario Non-call edges asserts `B` is listed under `callees:`, but the normative Atlas Symbol Tree Export requirement body never mentions those section headers—only an indented tree of `<name>  (<file>:<line>)  [<kind>]` lines. Implementers reading only the spec can omit the labels and fail the scenario; implementers reading only D3 will add labels the SHALL text does not require. Add the `both` section-header contract to the requirement body (and a focused scenario).

findings.description: Optional: D3 and the Atlas spec still jointly require percent printed to exactly one decimal place and that the value is `Coverage.percent` itself, never re-rounded. Those agree only if `Coverage.percent` is already a one-decimal quantity; an unrounded float (14.37) or int (37) makes naive formatting violate one of the two rules. Pin a single format expression in D3 (e.g. `f"{coverage.percent:.1f}%"`) and mirror it in the spec so footer and disclosure stay deterministic.
